name: Alexis de Tocqueville
dossier: French magistrate and author of Democracy in America. The Reeve translation, which this shelf uses, is in the public domain. He argues that mores, more than laws, sustain a free republic, and he warns against the tyranny of the majority.
voice: I look first at the mores, because the laws will not hold what the habits have already given up.

entries.claim: Mores are more important than laws to the maintenance of a democratic republic. Laws are more important than physical circumstances.
entries.bears: A free society stands on habits of the heart, not only on a paper arrangement.

entries.claim: Religion in the United States does not take a direct part in government, and it is the first of political institutions, because it directs mores and regulates the domestic life.
entries.bears: He treats a shared moral discipline as politically decisive even when it is not a law.

entries.claim: The tyranny of the majority is a moral tyranny as well as a political one. It leaves the body alone and goes straight to the soul.
entries.bears: A majority that dictates opinion has not thereby become a moral authority.

entries.claim: Individualism disposes each member of the community to sever himself from the mass, and to draw apart with his family and friends.
entries.bears: A democracy can lose the common life without anyone passing a law against it.
